page: Microsoft Azure D8pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by an 8-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features a dedicated CPU allocation with one thread per core, 32.0 GB of RAM, and 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU cache architecture includes 64 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 128 MB L3 cache. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and supports Premium Storage.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier memory performance, achieving a top-10% Passmark memory score. Single-threaded gzip compression is strong, placing in the top 25%. Most other compute and memory bandwidth metrics fall within the average range, including stress-ng CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and static web serving throughput. However, cryptographic operations show some weakness, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is also a bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 7B model ranking in the bottom 10%.

Given its ARM architecture and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the D8pds_v6 offers a resource-dense profile that is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads optimized for ARM64. The inclusion of 472 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage makes it highly suitable for database operations, web serving, and general-purpose application hosting. It is less suited for heavy cryptographic tasks or complex LLM inference workloads due to specific benchmark limitations in those areas.
description: Microsoft Azure D8pds_v6 is an ARM64-based virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated physical cores powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM and 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, offering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers top-tier memory performance, with its Passmark memory score ranking in the top 10%, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression. While general compute, web serving, and database benchmarks perform in the average tier, cryptographic operations and large-model LLM inference show relative performance weaknesses. The combination of dedicated ARM cores and fast local storage makes the D8pds_v6 a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for general-purpose applications, web hosting, and database workloads optimized for ARM architectures.
